key_facts: The UK's Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC) proposed that employees should legally be able to find out what their colleagues earn, with employers required to respond to questionnaires about colleagues' pay to reduce pay discrimination.

The EHRC also proposed that employers be prevented from asking about current salary when making job offers, since salary history can embed past discrimination into future pay; currently UK employers may ask but applicants are not obliged to answer.

key_facts: Households in council tax bands A to D in England will receive a £100 "Household Energy Payment", funded by extra tax on banks, paid directly into bank accounts; Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland will receive equivalent funding and decide whether to pass on the payment.

key_facts: The Federal Reserve held its policy rate steady at 3.75%-4% on Wednesday, with a 10-2 vote; the range was set in September, when policymakers unanimously raised rates for the first time since 2023. Inflation remains 'elevated' and above the 2% target, with no recent progress toward it. Dissenters Lisa D. Cook (her first-ever dissent) and Beth M. Hammack favored a quarter-point increase.

Chairman Kevin Warsh said the Fed will hold eight meetings in 2027, one of which will focus exclusively on broad monetary policy strategy without a rate vote; starting in 2028, two meetings per year will be dedicated to such strategy sessions. Warsh said politics played no role in the decision, days before the midterm elections.

Since September, price pressures have broadened after shocks from Trump's tariffs and the U.S.-Israel war with Iran, with energy prices rising sharply. Wage gains have lagged inflation, and U.S. government borrowing costs have risen sharply. Warsh said credit conditions have tightened for some businesses and households, though he was 'unwilling and unable' to call overall financial conditions tight.
importance_reason: Решение ФРС по ставке — прямой якорь важности 5 по калибровке.

The OBR downgraded UK growth forecast for next year to 1%; the cash ISA allowance cut from £20,000 to £12,000 will be axed, and the basic-rate tax on savings and property income rises to 24% from April 2027. Defence spending and welfare decisions are deferred to next year's spending review.

key_facts: The OBR's latest official forecast says soaring energy prices linked to the US-Iran war will dent UK growth in the short term, push up inflation and leave living standards in a "grim" place. OBR raised its 2026 growth forecast but cut its 2027 forecast from 1.6% to 1%.

The OBR now expects inflation to peak at 3.8% in 2027 and average 3.4% next year before falling to the Bank of England's 2% target towards the end of the decade. Rates are currently at 3.75%, and the OBR now forecasts they could rise to as high as 4.5% in coming years, after previously forecasting two cuts this year. The Bank is widely expected to raise rates next week.

Petrol averages almost £1.73 per litre and diesel near £1.99. Real household disposable income is forecast to grow from 2027 but by less than previously thought; the OBR forecasts a dip in living standards next year. Government debt interest spending is set to rise, and borrowing is forecast to increase each year by more than previously expected.

Chancellor John Healey announced cost-of-living measures he said would offer "breathing space" to households; Pantheon Macroeconomics called them "small beer given the surge in inflation we expect over the winter." The OBR said there remains "significant uncertainty" in its forecasts.
importance_reason: Official OBR forecast with a sharp downgrade to 2027 growth, a higher inflation peak and higher expected rates, directly tied to the energy shock; a near-certain BoE hike is also flagged.

key_facts: The Federal Reserve voted on Wednesday to hold its benchmark interest rate steady, as markets had widely expected. The FOMC said the accumulation of more information will help determine the policy stance needed for a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal.

Two FOMC members dissented: Governor Lisa Cook, whose dissent from a rate vote was described as a surprise since she had not dissented on rate votes since taking her seat in 2022, and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack.

Starting in 2027, the FOMC will still hold eight meetings, but one will not include a rate vote or post-meeting statement; the number of 'strategy' meetings will rise to two, leaving six meetings for rate adjustments outside emergency meetings. Post-meeting press conferences were shortened to about half an hour, with reporters limited to one question each, and seating order was changed.
